songs.name: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy '71 show with scorching Hard To Handle and tight jam flow
ai_show_review.blurb: The set delivers standout performances of Wharf Rat, Hard To Handle, The Other One and Cumberland Blues, all rendered with crisp soundboard clarity. Pigpen’s organ and harmonica drive the band while Bill Kreutzmann fuels the jams with fiery drum work.
ai_show_review.review: April 21, 1971 at the Rhode Island Auditorium captures the Dead in a rare burst of pure momentum. From the opening Casey Jones through a seamless Truckin' → Drums → The Other One segue, the band rides a high‑octane wave that never loses its groove. Jerry Garcia’s lead on Wharf Rat sparkles, his solo on Hard To Handle is blistering, and his vocals stay front‑and‑center throughout. Phil Lesh “flies through” the set with driving bass lines that lock in perfectly on Cumberland Blues and during the extended jams. Ron "Pigpen" McKernan provides a powerful backbone on organ, harmonica and vocals, especially evident in the soulful rendition of Wharf Rat. Bill Kreutzmann is literally on fire, adding wild‑man drum breaks that lift each improvisational peak. The second set keeps the momentum alive with a tight Bertha → Sugar Magnolia transition, a double Not Fade Away sandwich around Goin’ Down The Road Feeling Bad, and an uplifting encore featuring Uncle John’s Band and Johnny B. Goode. The Kaplan soundboard capture (gd71-04-21.sbd.kaplan.8227.sbeok.shnf) preserves every nuance, delivering an excellent, crisp listening experience that lets the night’s energy shine through.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard source with crystal‑clear clarity, minimal hiss and full capture of the high‑energy performance.
